items.title: Grover Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, February 13, 1996
items.q: I’ve been in and out of this band for about 35 years, in one capacity or another. Most of my time I spent as lead trombone player. Then I came back in 1980 when the old man got sick, and I was helping.

ctx.x: It’s almost a tradition with the Basie band to be able to generate excitement and swing but so soft and slow.

Oh, yeah. That’s a lesson that, well this band is kind of an apprenticeship for somebody like me. I’ve been in and out of this band for about 35 years, in one capacity or another. Most of my time I spent as lead trombone player. Then I came back in 1980 when the old man got sick, and I was helping. I was playing, but at the same time, you know I was starting to be his hands and arms and legs and I had to even help him think you know. Because he’d had a couple of strokes and all that, and he could get a little…
I should explain to our viewers that you have taken over the Basie band, it’s about eight months now?
